summary: @ornikar/babel-preset-react ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime to execute a 727KB obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a trivial Babel React preset — index.js is a 12-line re-export of @babel/preset-react — but package.json declares a preinstall hook that runs setup.mjs. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime (v1.3.13) from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js via execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')], {cwd: D}). math_init.js is a 727KB minified/obfuscated JavaScript file with hex-named identifiers (_0xNNNN) and string-array lookup patterns; it is not referenced from index.js and is only reachable through the Bun-based execution path. The wrapper (setup.mjs) is itself obfuscated. The declared package purpose (a Babel preset) has no legitimate need for the Bun runtime or a 727KB opaque sibling payload. The manifest declares repository ornikar/shared-configs, whose legitimate upstream package is a simple preset re-export with no preinstall hook and no such payload, indicating this tarball is a compromised or impersonating publish under the @ornikar scope. On npm install, arbitrary attacker-controlled code runs on the installer's machine via the alternate-runtime dropper path, bypassing scanners that only inspect Node-executed code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
